published_statement: p.13: 'Consider a region between Casimir plates at z = +-L/2 in otherwise flat spacetime and an inertial trajectory parallel to the plates. Let l be the distance from this trajectory to the nearest plate in the t = 0 surface. Then no experiment conducted along the trajectory in a time interval of less than 2l can possibly know about the existence of the plates; it should be as if the experiment was conducted in Minkowski space. In particular the quantum energy inequalities apply, and [as the energy density is supposed constant along the trajectory] (4) gives an a priori bound T00 >= -C/(2l)^4 ~ -3.17/(2l)^4 = -0.20/l^4. By comparison, the known value of the Casimir energy density for the massless minimally coupled scalar field is T00 = -pi^2/(1140 L^4) - (pi^2/(48 L^4))(3 - 2cos^2(pi z/L))/cos^4(pi z/L) which ranges between 3-7% of the bound as z varies in [-L/2, L/2].' p.14: the a priori bound 'also applies to all stationary (Hadamard) states of the system ... There remains an interesting question as to why the Casimir energy density is a comparatively small proportion of the allowed bound.' Eq.(4), p.11: rho >= -C/tau^4, 'C ~ 3.17', from Eq.(3) p.10, of which Fewster says 'The bound is known not to be optimal.'
published_hypotheses: P1 free massless MINIMALLY coupled real scalar field (the density quoted is for this field; Eq.(3) holds for m >= 0)
P2 ideal plates at z = +-L/2 with (Dirichlet) boundary conditions in otherwise flat spacetime -- the quoted density is the Dirichlet one (re-derived here from the Dirichlet image sum, B1-B4)
P3 inertial trajectory parallel to the plates at distance l from the nearer plate
P4 the energy density is constant along the trajectory (stationary state), so Eq.(4) applies with tau = 2l
P5 causal/locality argument: a measurement of duration < 2l cannot detect the plates, so the Minkowski QEI applies (basis: local covariance, ref [31], NAMED-NOT-READ)
P6 Hadamard states; the bound is state-independent and applies to all stationary Hadamard states of the plate system (p.14)
P7 Eq.(3), on which Eq.(4) and so the a priori bound rest, 'is known not to be optimal' (p.10) -- the 3-7% is a fraction of a valid, non-sharp bound

Against any sharper valid bound C_s <= C the ratio is R*C/C_s >= R. Saturation at the midpoint would require a sharp constant C_s = 0.2125 (1440) / 0.2143 (1140), i.e. C/14.9 (script E). RELABELLED BOUND: the withdrawn clause (achievable.py:41, restated :205; ledger.py:1998) is 'Casimir is THE FORD-ROMAN bound saturated'. Fewster's a priori bound is Eq.(4) -- the Fewster-Eveson Eq.(3) functional with the optimal clamped compactly-supported sampler over a window fixed at 2l by causality -- not Ford-Roman's Lorentzian -3/(32 pi^2 tau_0^4). Ford & Roman's own treatment (gr-qc/9510071 Sec. 2, READ in docket audit gr-qc_9510071.json) caps tau_0 <= 0.46 L precisely where the constant Casimir density EQUALS their Eq.(1) bound -- equality at the cap by construction. So Fewster's 3-7% does not refute 'saturated' in Ford-Roman's own sense; it shows that under a different, valid bound Casimir sits well inside. Recorded, not repaired.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. Fewster (2012) needed no empirical datum: the result is the ratio of a closed-form vacuum density (Dirichlet image sum, known since the 1970s) to a derived bound with a mathematical constant. Every input he used re-derives here; the only defect is a misprint (1140 for 1440), which moves the midpoint 6.76% -> 6.70% and leaves '3-7%' intact. So on Fewster's own statement nothing he lacked changes his conclusion -- evidence: script B4, B5, C1-C5. What WAS lacking then, and is not supplied by anything read here, is the SHARP 4D QEI constant: Eq.(3) is 'known not to be optimal', and a sharp constant can only raise the ratio (C_s <= C => ratio >= 3-7%). Saturation at the midpoint would need C_s = C/14.9. That missing quantity does not touch Fewster's sentence but DOES bear on the tree's stronger reading ('Casimir does not saturate the QEI', 'three per cent is not a wall'), and only in the direction against the tree. The other datum the tree implies -- a measured Casimir energy density -- does not exist: experiments measure force (docket audit casimir-force-measurements.json). Real (dispersive) plates move the density away from saturation, not toward it (Sopova-Ford, READ in that audit).
grade_evidence: Fewster's statement re-derives: C = 3.16986 (A1-A4), his minimal-coupling term exactly (B4), the ratio monotone from 6.70% (6.76% on his printed 1140) to 16/mu_1^4 = 3.196% at the plates (C1-C5) -- '3-7%' holds; 1140 is a misprint (B5), a discrepancy not a refutation. The tree's use is WIDER than the source in four named places, so NARROWED, not STANDS: (i) 'REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT' (achievable.py:205; bounds.py:341,418) -- a calculation, no measurement; (ii) 'Casimir' generically (achievable.py:205-214, ledger.py:1998-2001) for a Dirichlet minimally coupled scalar result; (iii) 'Saturation is not 3 %' (achievable.py:213) against a bound Fewster calls non-optimal -- against the sharp bound, saturation needs C_s = C/14.9 and is OPEN; (iv) the withdrawn claim names the FORD-ROMAN bound, which in Ford-Roman's own capped form (gr-qc/9510071, docket-READ) the Casimir density meets with equality at the cap. Not WRONG: no counterexample to the published statement, and the tree's withdrawal of 'Casimir saturates it' as an established fact stands (it was never shown); what narrows is 'REFUTED'. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no measured datum enters. Caveat on reading: this stage read the p.13-14 text through the docket's verbatim page-text record (alphaXiv quota exhausted, arXiv blocked).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree's sites say 'Casimir (massless minimally coupled Dirichlet scalar) sits at 3-7% of Fewster's a priori bound, which is not optimal', drop 'MEASUREMENT', and do not equate Fewster's bound with Ford-Roman's -- or a read source establishes a sharp 4D constant with C_s >> C/14.9 (so the density stays far from any valid bound). To WRONG (for the tree's reading, not Fewster's): a read source establishing a sharp constant near C/14.9 or smaller, i.e. a valid bound the Casimir density actually meets. To OPEN: if a fresh read of 1208.5399 p.13 contradicted the docket's transcription (re-read when alphaXiv quota resets).
